questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My wish was to go someplace different from where I usually attend the university - in Denmark. I think that the culture in the South of Europe is very different from ours - so I wanted to explore something new. Also, Bologna is very much a student city and the medium size of the city was also appealing to me. And of course the weather also drew me there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright - especially since I could talk to a lot of other Erasmus students, and we could help each other.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't think that I received any assistance - perhaps some e-mails!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very confusing - having to get to know a whole new system - but you figure it out along the way!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Luckily, it was easy for me - since I had a friend who stayed in Bologna, and who could give me some useful contacts!
But I do recommend searching for housing in good time - around March or April, if you go on exchange in the fall.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I don't think that you can live on campus in Bologna - so you don't have a choice. 
But a recommendation is to try to get housing inside the "walls" or not to far away from the "walls".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite expensive - this is the main downside.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is very relaxed in Bologna - you registrate during the fall, and you get the opportunity of trying out different courses before signing up for them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
I think that there was a student desk. 
Mostly, I just scrolled around on the main websites for the university - those are helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about not having everything in order in good time - Italy is not that organized, so deal with things as they come.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The difficulty of the courses depended very much of the professor. A MA course is not necessarily more difficult than a BA course - but can be. 
Overall, more easy than in Denmark - but you still need to put in effort to get through the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
We had a lot of lectures and no class teaching. 
I like the style in Denmark more, but it was a lot of fun to try out something different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BA course: Philosophy of Law 9 credits
BA course: Comparative Constitutionalism 9 credits
MA course: Corporate Law 6 credits
MA course: International and Transnational Civil Litigation 6 credits

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Philosophy of Law and Comparative Constitutionalism. 
Great teachers. 
Interesting courses! 
The exam type in Comparative Constitutionalism was very nice - I kind of enjoyed writing those papers on very interesting topics even though I stressed about it. 
Notice that Philosophy of Law requires more effort - it is an oral exam, and you need to know your stuff if you want to obtain a good grade.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When I arrived, I had to buy a duvet, sheets, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and drinks are cheap!
Put some money aside for making trips also.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Language courses. My roomies did choir.
But mostly you don't do activities that the university arrange - people mostly attend activities that the Erasmus network organizes!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I did not attend any activities as such at the university. 
But I attended a lot of social activities with the Erasmus network - can recommend!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
First of all, get to know the city. It is a great city with a lot of great restaurants and bars. Make sure to go to San Luca, and do hiking in the surrounding areas!
Also, do trips! I can really recommend Napoli, Verona, Lucca, and Firenze.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy - italian people are very welcoming. One advice would be to try and learn the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
The most easy one would be to live with italian people. 
Other tips: 
Take courses with italian students. 
Make conversation in the streets at aperitivo time or in bars.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
In Denmark, we have a lot of structure. 
They don't have that in Italy. 
Can be both an advantage and a challenge. 
Also, the way things work in the university is very different - you have to get used to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
A lot of life in the city at all times of the day and at any time of the year. The Italian people have a great spirit, and you should definitely spend much time just hanging with your friends for an Aperol in the afternoon and going to restaurants at night. 
Also, so much culture and history to explore in this country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Search for housing in good time. 
2. Arrive a bit before the courses at the university begins - so that you have time to get to know and explore the city and meet new people in advance. 
3. Do not stress about not having things in order - in Italy things take time and be prepared that some things will be delayed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to study a bit during the semester so that you won't be too stressed when the exams get close.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting new friends from all around Europe. 
Exploring a new culture - Bologna is an amazing city to live in and has that Italian vibe. 
Exploring the country - there are endless opportunities on going on different trips.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was challenging having the courses in English - I was not used to that, but I like this challenge and gained a lot from it. Also, I think I should have taken a bit more time to be by myself - it is exhausting to settle in a new city not knowing anyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
